citeAs: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (2025). WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal. arXiv:2501.07572.
creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal, evaluating their capacity to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It comprises 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages, with both single-source and multi-source QA types in English and Chinese.
name: WebWalkerQA
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each QA pair is first annotated by GPT-4o and then verified/calibrated by human annotators (two-stage process per item).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Crowd-sourced human annotators (platform not specified); GPT-4o for initial LLM-based annotation
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy: (1) LLM-based annotation using GPT-4o to generate synthetic QA pairs based on gathered page information, constructing both multi-source and single-source query types, with verification and filtering for legitimate queries retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities; (2) Human annotation where crowd-sourced human annotators rewrite and calibrate questions and answers to ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent.
rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy was employed. First, official websites were traversed recursively to collect information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages. Root pages were identified through Google search using keywords such as "conference official website" or "game official website", followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of university computer science departments were chosen. Queries were constructed based on page information, then verified and filtered for legitimate queries. GPT-4o performed initial annotations, followed by crowd-sourced human annotators conducting quality control and filtering.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites from four domains: conference, organization, education, and game. Web pages were collected by recursively traversing official websites and collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages. Web page content was extracted in Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool.
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. The dataset only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons, not visual modalities such as screenshots. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, which may cause answers to become outdated over time.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Web pages were parsed into Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool. Clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs were extracted using Beautiful Soup. Queries were filtered to retain only QA pairs with short answers containing entities, and those deviating from natural, human-like phrasing were removed.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark highlights the importance of deep, vertical exploration in web-based tasks, paving the way for more scalable and reliable LLM-based information retrieval integrated with RAG. It addresses the limitation of traditional search engines that perform only horizontal searches and may not effectively trace deeper content embedded within websites.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking LLMs on web traversal tasks; evaluating the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically; evaluating RAG systems on deep information retrieval; assessing multi-step information-seeking capabilities of LLM-based agents in real-world web scenarios.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o (OpenAI) was used for initial annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs and verify/filter queries. GPT-4 was used as the evaluator to determine correctness of responses using CoT prompting. The ai4crawl tool was used to extract web pages in Markdown-like format. Beautiful Soup was used to extract clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs.
